classification.habit: Small perennial hairy herb with long creeping rhizome; alpine Himalaya 3000–5000 m
classification.habitat: Moist rocky crevices and alpine slopes of the Himalaya at about 3000–5000 m.
classification.distribution: North-western to eastern Himalaya, from Kashmir to Sikkim; heavily collected from the wild and now threatened.

identification.description: Sub-cylindrical grayish-brown rhizomes marked with prominent circular leaf-scars and stem remnants, porous white internal fracture, intensely bitter persistent taste.
identification.whole_plant: Small, more or less hairy perennial herb with a long creeping rhizome, a rosette of basal leaves and a short flowering spike.
identification.root: Roots thin, cylindrical, 5–10 cm long, dusty grey, mostly attached to the rhizome; inner surface black with whitish xylem; taste bitter.
identification.stem: Rhizome 2.5–8 cm long and 4–8 mm thick, subcylindrical, greyish-brown, rough with longitudinal wrinkles and circular scars, ending in a bud with a tuft of leaves; fracture short, taste bitter.
identification.leaf: Leaves mostly basal, spathulate, sharply serrate, narrowed into a winged stalk.
identification.flower: Small whitish or pale blue-purple flowers crowded in a dense terminal spike, with long projecting stamens.
identification.fruit: Small ovoid capsule containing many seeds.
identification.seed: Minute, numerous seeds with a loose, transparent, net-like coat.
identification_points: Sub-cylindrical grayish-brown rhizomes marked with prominent circular leaf-scars and stem remnants, porous white internal fracture, intensely bitter persistent taste.

therapeutics.precautions: Bhedana in larger doses; may cause griping and loose stools. Commonly adulterated or substituted with Gentiana kurroo, so authenticate the rhizome.
therapeutics.contraindications: Pregnancy, Atisara, marked Vata predominance and debility (Laghu-Ruksha, Bhedana drug).

shlokas:
कट्वी तु कटुका तिक्ता कृष्णभेदा कटम्भरा ।
अशोका मत्स्यशकला चक्राङ्गी शकुलादनी ।
मत्स्यपित्ता काण्डरुहा रोहिणी कटुरोहिणी ॥१३४॥

कट्वी तु कटुका पाके तिक्ता रूक्षा हिमा लघुः ।
भेदिनी दीपनी हृद्या कफपित्तज्वरापहा ।
प्रमेहश्वासकासास्रदाहकुष्ठकृमिप्रणुत् ॥१३५॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The bitter principles are iridoid glycosides (picrosides and kutkoside, together called kutkin), which are the main markers of the rhizome.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Used in liver cleansing, detox, and skin conditions.
recognized_uses: Traditional hepatoprotective drug in Kamala and liver disorders
Bitter for fever and loss of appetite
Key ingredient of Arogyavardhini Vati and Tiktaka Ghrita
modern_information.safety_notes: Generally tolerated in pharmacopoeial doses; higher doses act as a purgative. Wild supply is threatened and adulteration is common.

Formulations: Arogyavardhini Vati, Tiktaka Ghrita, Mahatiktaka Ghrita (API)
